_note: The oldest category and the least deserved: water, wind, fire and the ground itself, landing where the machine draws them. Every event here carries sited: true -- the card, the diary and the ledger name the region -- and the cooldowns run ten to eighteen months because the weather has seasons. river_flood and heat_wave moved here at T9 when climate.json retired; they are the category's two originals.

events.name: The sea takes the front row
events.summary: The surge put two metres of sea into streets that had been promised a decade more, and the marina is where the promenade was. The sea wall's plans are five years old and uncosted, and the tide tables say the next one is a matter of when.
events.speaker_line: The sea took streets we promised a decade, plans for the wall sit uncosted, and the tide tables say this was a rehearsal.

choices.label: Build it higher
choices.summary: The wall goes to the new figure and the contracts go to the same four firms, at a speed nobody audits until it is over. The coast is safe for the length of the chart and the interior pays for scenery it cannot see.

choices.label: Buy the front row out
choices.summary: The state buys the seafront street by street and lets the beach have it back. The owners are made whole once; the town loses its postcard, its season and its tax base in the same Gazette.

choices.label: Repair to the old line
choices.summary: The wall goes back to the height that failed and the argument goes back to the committee that has held it for a decade. The next surge is booked by the tide tables, not the committee.

events.name: The fire week
events.summary: The fire ran eight kilometres in the first afternoon and took the village the evacuation plan had at the bottom of its second page. It is out now, and the question at the desk is whether the burned acres are replanted, grazed or argued over.
events.speaker_line: Fire ran eight kilometres in an afternoon and outgrew the evacuation plan's second page, and now we must decide what grows back.

choices.label: Reforest to the plan
choices.summary: Twenty years of trees planted in twelve months of contracts. The hills are green on the schedule, the grazing is closed while it happens, and the grazers are at the ministry by the second month.

choices.label: Clear the fuel and open the hills
choices.summary: Firebreaks, controlled burns and the hill farms back on land the trees had. The fire service calls it fuel management; the walking clubs call it the end of the woods, and both write to you.

choices.label: Let the scrub decide
choices.summary: It decides for the fast cheap species and for the next fire's fuel. The valley keeps the view and loses the shade, and the second part is the one the summer proves.

events.name: The drought order
events.summary: The reservoir is at the level at which the prefect signs the order, and the farmers' union is at the ministry before the ink is. Hosepipe bans, irrigation cuts, and a harvest that depends on a third cut of grass the grass will not make.
events.speaker_line: The reservoir has reached the level where an order gets signed, the farmers are already at the ministry, and the grass will not make a third cut.

choices.label: Sign the order as written
choices.summary: The towns keep their water and the fields carry the cut. The harvest comes in smaller by the ministry's own estimate, which the union reads aloud at every market from here to autumn.

choices.label: Carry the towns instead
choices.summary: The irrigation holds and the tankers run to the villages the mains were never extended to. The bill lands on the interior line at summer rates and the cities read about it in the same sentence as their taps.

choices.label: Wait for rain
choices.summary: The forecast says three weeks and the fodder says twelve days. Somebody's arithmetic is wrong, and the union has already decided whose.

events.name: The crossing came down
events.summary: The span came down in the night with nobody on it, which is the only kind thing the year has done. The crossing carried nine thousand vehicles a day, the detour costs an hour and a half, and the file on the repairs that slipped four times is a court exhibit now.
events.speaker_line: The crossing came down empty at night, nine thousand vehicles a day now lose an hour and a half, and the repair file is a court exhibit.

choices.label: Commission the crossing now
choices.summary: A design-and-build contract is signed in six weeks on a site the coroner has not released, and the crossing opens in three years. The auditor opens before that, which is the price of the speed.

choices.label: Ferry and detour
choices.summary: The ferry is running by Friday and the auditor is running by Monday, and the valley spends a decade on a road built for a summer. The money is small; the schedule is permanent.

choices.label: Wait for the inquiry
choices.summary: It reports in fourteen months with three recommendations and a resignation, and the detour is a habit by then. Habits are taxes the valley pays without an invoice.

events.name: The levee that was on the list
events.summary: The levee failed at the third-highest flood of the decade, in the reach every inspection since the last one has marked for strengthening. The water is in the villages behind it and the reports are in the ministry, filed by year, all of them right.
events.speaker_line: Every inspection since the last one marked that levee for strengthening, and now the water is in the villages and the files are in the ministry, all of them right.

choices.label: Say the state knew
choices.summary: The minister reads the inspection history to the cameras, which is either the end of a career or the beginning of a programme. The strengthening starts at the failed reach and the budget line finally exists, with the ministry's initials on it.

choices.label: Call it an unprecedented event
choices.summary: The third-highest flood in a decade is unprecedented in the way the ministry needs it to be. The repairs are patched to the old line and the next inspection is scheduled for after the next flood.

choices.label: Compensate and move on
choices.summary: The claims are paid from the reserve at the speed reserves pay, and the levee is rebuilt to the height it failed at. The villages are grateful twice: for the money, and later for knowing exactly what the state thinks a village is worth.

events.name: The twelve-day freeze
events.summary: The cold came early and stayed, the grid is at the peak the interconnects were built for, and the mortality register moves in figures nobody publishes weekly. The schools are closed where the boilers are old, which is a map of everything else.
events.speaker_line: Cold came early and stayed, the grid is at the peak it was built for, and the deaths are counted in figures nobody wants published.

choices.label: Pay whatever the peak costs
choices.summary: The interconnects buy from wherever the wind is and the bill is settled in the spring, at the rate a cold week costs when it is bought warm. The hospitals hold their ward temperatures and the operator keeps the receipts.

choices.label: Ask industry to hold its peak
choices.summary: The furnaces cool by roster for twelve nights. The grid holds, the night shifts are paid anyway, and the mills' accountants spend January explaining February to their opposite numbers.

choices.label: Let the price do it
choices.summary: The price does it. The old houses with the old boilers find out what a cold week costs at the new tariff, and the mortality register finds out in March.

events.name: The hillside moved
events.summary: The hill above the village moved after nine days of rain, taking the road, the rail ballast and an argument about drainage the two communes have been having since the last time. Nobody died; forty houses are on the wrong side of a geologist's line now.
events.speaker_line: Nine days of rain moved the hill, nobody died, and forty houses now sit on the wrong side of the geologist's line.

choices.label: Build the drainage the file named
choices.summary: The scheme in the annex is built as drawn, which ends the argument by ending the hill's interest in it. The communes split the maintenance and resume the argument on schedule.

choices.label: Redraw the line and buy the forty
choices.summary: The hazard line is redrawn honestly and the forty houses are bought at pre-slide values. The village moves up the hill intact, which no plan dared promise, and the old street becomes a meadow with a history.

choices.label: Clear the road and watch the hill
choices.summary: The road opens in a month with the monitoring stakes in beside it. The geologist's line stays a sentence in an annex until the hill moves again, and the annex is where the forty houses will still be living.

events.name: The eleven seconds
events.summary: It lasted eleven seconds and the old town took most of them. The schools that were retrofitted are the ones standing, which is the whole argument, and the camps in the squares are the whole emergency, and the aftershock forecast keeps them full.
events.speaker_line: Eleven seconds and the old town took most of them, and the camps in the squares are the emergency now.

choices.label: House the camps before winter
choices.summary: Modular housing on the parade grounds by the month's end, the army erecting it and the prefect counting it. The camps empty on a schedule, which no disaster plan has ever dared promise.

choices.label: Condemn and clear the old town
choices.summary: The unsafe orders go out in the week and the demolition goes in by the autumn. The rebuild is a decade and the argument about the facades is a career, and both start in the spring.

choices.label: Insure and improvise
choices.summary: The claims are processed at the speed the claims office has and the camps empty when they empty. The retrofit programme is announced in the spring, funded in the autumn and audited never.

events.name: The river breaks its banks
events.summary: Three days of rain and the valley is a lake. Two towns are cut off, the rail line is under water, and the prefect's damage list runs to forty communes. The works are not in question; whose answer it is, is.
events.speaker_line: Three days of rain and the valley is a lake, two towns cut off, and the only real question is whose answer it is.

choices.label: Repair by decree
choices.summary: The levees go back where the engineers draw the line, not where the communes asked, and the contracts are signed before the water has finished going down. The payroll is real; so is the memory of not being asked.

choices.label: Appeal for EU solidarity
choices.summary: The Union's solidarity fund answers in nine months, if it answers. The appeal photographs well in the capital; in the valley it reads as a government waiting for Brussels while the cellars are still wet.

choices.label: Let the water go down first
choices.summary: The assessment comes first, the cameras leave, and by the time the plan is ready the money's best use has gone with the water. The valley keeps the mud and the memory.

events.name: The heat does not break
events.summary: The fourteenth day over forty, the mortality figures moving, and the hospitals deferring surgery to hold the evening peak. Nobody in the country needs telling where summers like this one come from.
events.speaker_line: Fourteenth day of it, hospitals are deferring surgery, and the mortality figures are moving in a direction nobody can ignore.

choices.label: Declare a health emergency
choices.summary: The wards reopen, the street-by-street visits to the elderly start tomorrow, and the deferrals stop. The health line carries the bill for the rest of the term, and business carries the midday stop.

choices.label: Cool the cities
choices.summary: Cooling rooms in every district, mist over the squares, the buses free between noon and four. The cities call it leadership; the countryside notes where the shade went up.

choices.label: Call it weather
choices.summary: It breaks in the end; summers always have. The excess deaths will be a line in a winter report, and the people they name will not be reading it.
